author: Anonymous
occasion: Christians have been arrested at Rome for refusing orders to sacrifice to idols and are brought before the Roman prefect Rusticus. The work preserves their interrogation, confession, condemnation and death for the faithful.
argument: Justin is ordered to obey the gods and the emperors but answers that obedience to Jesus Christ is blameless, and summarizes Christian belief in one creator God and in Christ foretold by the prophets. Pressed about Christian meetings, he denies a single gathering place because God is not confined to place, and says he teaches the words of truth to visitors at his lodging in Rome. Each of the other prisoners in turn declares himself or herself a Christian and explains the source of that allegiance, whether parents, Christ, or prior faith. Ordered finally to sacrifice together and threatened with merciless punishment, Justin and the others refuse to move from true worship to impiety, affirm hope of heavenly reward and salvation at Christ's judgment seat, and are therefore sentenced to be scourged and beheaded, which is carried out and followed by burial by fellow believers.

outline.move: Narrator sets impious edicts compelling Christians to sacrifice and the arrest and bringing of the holy men before Rusticus, prefect of Rome.
Rusticus interrogates Justin about obedience, philosophical teachings, and doctrine, and Justin confesses faith in the one creator God and in Jesus Christ foretold by the prophets.

Rusticus presses Justin about where Christians meet and where he gathers disciples, and Justin names his lodging above Martinus' bath, denies knowing any other assembly, and declares he is a Christian.
Rusticus examines Chariton, Charito, Euelpistus, Hierax, Paeon and Liberianus one by one, each confesses to being a Christian and states parentage, home, or how they became Christian.

Rusticus tests Justin on ascent to heaven after scourging and beheading, then demands joint sacrifice, the prisoners refuse and accept punishment for salvation, and Rusticus sentences those who will not sacrifice to scourging and death by the sword.
The martyrs glorify God, are beheaded at the usual place, complete their witness in confession of the Savior, and are secretly buried by believers, closing with a doxology to Christ.

cast.name: Rusticus
cast.who: Roman prefect of Rome who interrogates and sentences the prisoners.

cast.name: Justin
cast.who: Christian teacher in Rome, chief spokesman, lodges above a bathhouse and teaches visitors.

cast.name: Chariton
cast.who: One of Justin's companions, declares he is a Christian by God's command.

cast.name: Charito
cast.who: Female companion, declares she is a Christian by God's gift.

cast.name: Euelpistus
cast.who: Caesar's slave from Cappadocia, freed by Christ and sharing the same hope by Christ's grace; listened gladly to Justin's words but received being a Christian from his parents.

cast.name: Hierax
cast.who: Companion from Iconium in Phrygia; says Christ is our true father and faith in him our mother, his earthly parents having died.

cast.name: Paeon
cast.who: Companion standing by who declares he received the confession from his parents.

cast.name: Liberianus
cast.who: Last companion examined, declares he worships the only true God.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: Savior, Son and Servant of God, teacher foretold by the prophets and future judge.

cast.name: Martinus son of Timothinus
cast.who: Man above whose bathhouse Justin lodges in Rome; not a Christian speaker.

voices.speaker: Narrator
voices.how_marked: third-person narrative without quotation formula, including narrator-framed sentence report in section 5 with Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος ἀπεφήνατο λέγων and Οἱ μὴ βουληθέντες...

voices.speaker: Rusticus the prefect
voices.how_marked: formulae such as Ῥουστικὸς ὁ ἔπαρχος εἶπεν / λέγει πρὸς τὸν Ἰουστῖνον; in section 5 his final sentencing speech is embedded in narrator's report with ἀπεφήνατο λέγων, with narrator framing the transition

voices.speaker: Justin
voices.how_marked: formula Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν in reply to the prefect

voices.speaker: Chariton, Charito, Euelpistus, Hierax, Paeon, Liberianus individually
voices.how_marked: name plus εἶπε / ἀπεκρίνατο, e.g. Χαρίτων εἶπε, Εὐέλπιστος ἀπεκρίνατο

voices.speaker: The other martyrs together
voices.how_marked: ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ μάρτυρες εἶπον

key_terms.sense: in this work a person loyal to Christ and to the one God, confessed openly before a judge even under death threat
the one creator of all things worshipped by Christians, contrasted with so-called gods / idols
right loyalty and worship toward the true God, treated as incompatible with sacrificing
a man-made object of pagan cult, called empty, to which sacrifice is demanded
to offer cultic sacrifice to gods or idols, the demanded act the Christians refuse
a teaching, school position, or reasoned account; Justin claims to follow the true ones, those of the Christians
the content of what Christians revere and follow about God and Christ
open declaration I am a Christian received from parents or held as good confession
the completed public witness sealed by suffering and death in confession of the Savior
rescue through punished suffering for Christ, leading to heavenly dwelling and boldness at judgment

scripture: No biblical book is named or quoted verbatim; there is only a general appeal to what was foretold by the prophets about Christ's coming among humans. No Psalm numbering or Vulgate/LXX book-title issue arises in this text; if prophets are later cited explicitly, cite in modern form by common English book and chapter-verse.
uncertain: Date of composition versus date of events: the trial points to the prefecture of Junius Rusticus under Marcus Aurelius, traditionally c. 165, but the date and redaction history of this Acts text cannot be established from the text alone.
Authorship and source of the court record: whether any part derives from official minutes or is wholly later composition cannot be established from the text alone.
Identity of minor names and places: Martinus, Timothinus and his bathhouse, Cappadocia, Iconium of Phrygia, and the usual place of execution are named without further detail.
Which emperors or imperial order are meant by kings, emperor and the emperor's command is not specified in the text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Martinus son of Timothinus ... not a Christian speaker
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐγὼ ἐπάνω μένω τινὸς Μαρτίνου τοῦ Τιμοθίνου βαλανείου
_unresolved_facts.fix: Martinus son of Timothinus: man whose bathhouse is above which Justin lodges in Rome; text says nothing about whether he is Christian or speaks.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὡς εἰσαχθέντων πρὸ τοῦ βήματος Ῥουστικὸς ὁ ἔπαρχος εἶπε...
_unresolved_facts.fix: Narrator: sections ["1", "2", "5", "6"] — the narrator also provides the transition in section 2 (Ὡς εἰσαχθέντων...), not just sections 1, 5, 6.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Πρῶτον πείσθητι τοῖς θεοῖς...
_unresolved_facts.fix: Rusticus the prefect: sections ["2", "3", "4", "5"] — but note he also speaks in the transition at the start of section 2 (Ὡς εἰσαχθέντων...), and the brief's claim that section 5 has "narrator framing the transition" obscures that Rusticus's sentencing speech in section 5 is directly quoted within the narrator's report, not merely embedded without his voice.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Justin is ordered to obey the gods and the emperors
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Πρῶτον πείσθητι τοῖς θεοῖς καὶ ὑπάκουσον τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Justin is ordered to obey the gods and obey the kings (τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν), not "emperors" — the Greek uses βασιλεῦσιν (kings), not αὐτοκράτορσιν or similar. The emperor is referred to later as αὐτοκράτορος in the sentencing.

_unresolved_facts.claim: each of the other prisoners in turn declares himself or herself a Christian and explains the source of that allegiance, whether parents, Christ, or prior faith
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Λιβεριανὸς εἶπε· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι· εὐσεβῶ γὰρ καὶ προσκυνῶ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν
_unresolved_facts.fix: each of the other prisoners in turn declares himself or herself a Christian and explains the source of that allegiance or their worship of God — Liberianus does not state a source of allegiance (parents, Christ, or prior faith), but rather states that he worships the only true God.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Rusticus tests Justin on ascent to heaven after scourging and beheading
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐὰν μαστιγωθεὶς ἀποκεφαλισθῇς, πέπεισαι ὅτι μέλλεις ἀναβαίνειν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν;
_unresolved_facts.fix: Rusticus tests Justin on whether he is persuaded he will ascend to heaven if he is scourged and beheaded — the conditional "if" (ἐὰν) is important; Rusticus is not asserting this will happen but posing a hypothetical to test Justin's conviction.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the prisoners refuse and accept punishment for salvation
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἃν εὐχῆς ἔχωμεν διὰ τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τιμωρηθέντες σωθῆναι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Justin expresses hope/wish (Ἃν εὐχῆς ἔχωμεν, "if we have a prayer") that through punishment they may be saved; the others say "Do what you will. We are Christians and do not sacrifice to idols." — they do not explicitly "accept punishment for salvation" as a stated motive; Justin frames punishment as potential means to salvation, while the others simply refuse.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jesus Christ ... who: Savior, Son and Servant of God
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jesus Christ: Savior, Son and Child/Servant (παῖς) of God — "Servant" is a possible translation of παῖς, but "Son" (θεοῦ υἱὸν) is also explicitly used later in section 2. The brief conflates two distinct designations: παῖς (child/servant) and υἱός (son).
